title.title: The Correspondence of the Yarnall family

msIdentifier.institution: Friends Historical Library of Swarthmore College

projectDesc.p: The correspondence of Quaker minister Esther Roberts Hunt Collins is stored at the Friends Historical Library of Swarthmore College. With the generous support of H. David and Joyce E. Hunt, Library staff scanned and transcribed these letters in 2024 and encoded the text in TEI.

div.p: We have lately been favored with the acceptable company of our friends William Blakely and Jonathan Kirkbride, who visited the meetings in this neighborhood and are now gone on a visit to Eggharbour. And by them and our friends lately returned, I heard from you and was glad to hear of your welfare, except James, who by their account is not so well, of his complaint in his throat. And that you have rather concluded to go to the Doctor, which I expect you have—with myself had—under serious consideration, which I still hope may be the case and not move until you are convinced it may be for right and for the best.

I feel rather more than a freedom to inform of J. Kirkbride’s exercise on the occasion, and of instances of the like complaint to his knowledge were people of delicate constitutions, the operation hath been more than they could survive, and one of a strong one and able to bear it had it done and got well. Another that did not feel willing to have them taken out was after a time favored to have them break and run out, and get well.

We are much favored this fall in this neighborhood, it being a pretty general time of health except colds. I am myself at present complaining with one, also Elizabeth Collins, but were both out today at the burial of Issac Haines, the elder who hath been for many months confined with a dropsical complaint. And after the funeral come home with Joshua and Lydia Stokes to stay a day or two, who are desirous with myself to see thee over when its convenient. Our friends and relations about Westfield have been very sickly. Cousin Benjamin and Henry Warrington have both been ill so that Henry did not pass his second meeting. Brother Joseph and Hannah Buzby have lately been over to see us and have since heard that he is so he gets to meeting.

closer.salute: With love I conclude to you in which Joshua and Lydia unites, from thy affectionate Mother,

postscript.label: P.S.
postscript.p: If we are not likely to have a visit soon a letter will be very acceptable
